results.description:
<<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT id="1a717a65cc18848b">>>
Source: Web Search
---
I've heard various reports over the years saying that by the fall of 1993, Nirvana's popularity was starting to dwindle a bit and that In Utero didn't sell as many copies as the band and record company had hoped for upon release. I've also heard a few reports saying that Pearl Jam was becoming more popular than Nirvana by that point since they sold an astronomically high number of copies of their second album Vs. that same fall. It seems like people were essentially growing tired of Nirvana by that point, but then fast forward several months to Kurt's death and sales of In Utero picked up quickly after that and Nirvana's fame and legacy was cemented in an indelible way.
<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT id="1a717a65cc18848b">>>
